sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Our most capable model for complex tasks and teacher for model distillation
sources.evidence: Dated April 30, 2025 and announces general availability of Nova Premier, including us.amazon.nova-premier-v1:0. Specifies one-million-token context, text/image/video inputs excluding audio, tool workflows and distillation. Places Premier alongside non-reasoning models.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Exact eight-page Premier report establishes text/image/video processing, one-million-token context, function calling and distillation. It reports benchmarks, not total/active parameter counts or dense-versus-MoE topology. The older assets.amazon.science URL returned 404; the CDN PDF was accessible.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Original family report covers Pro, Lite, Micro, Canvas and Reel; Premier is not included. It describes the three understanding siblings as Transformer-based but gives no Premier parameter or topology disclosure. Sibling details are not transferred to Premier.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: Later 26-page report explicitly compares Nova 1 Premier in benchmark tables and describes Nova 2 hybrid extended thinking. It does not disclose total/active counts or dense/MoE topology for Premier. Table 3 marks Premier audio capability unsupported.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier — AWS AI Service Cards
sources.evidence: Service card explicitly covers all four models as of April 30, 2025. Its design section says Nova FMs perform token inference using transformer-based generative machine learning. It establishes multimodal text output, agentic/API workflows, Premier as teacher, and AWS service terms.

sources.title: What is Amazon Nova? — Version 1 model specifications
sources.evidence: Exact Premier column identifies amazon.nova-premier-v1:0, 1M context, text/image/video input and text output. Lists documents among Premier inputs and requires API access through Bedrock. Last-documented specifications do not prove endpoint operation today.

sources.title: Complete request schema — Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Although the shared JSON example contains audio and reasoningConfig, the parameter-specific explanation restricts reasoningConfig to Amazon Nova Pro and Amazon Nova Lite only. Premier is excluded. The toolConfig field defines function/tool calling.

sources.title: Document understanding — Amazon Nova Version 1
sources.evidence: Explicitly lists Lite, Pro and Premier as multimodal understanding models that interpret text and visual content in whole documents, including PDFs. Generic 1–2M context language is less specific than the exact Premier model table and is not used to expand its context.

sources.title: Iterative Training — Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: States Amazon Nova weights are proprietary and customized checkpoints remain in escrow S3 buckets in AWS-managed accounts. Managed customization is not a public weight release; examples use a different Nova variant, so this supplies only family ownership/access policy.

sources.title: AWS Service Terms
sources.evidence: Defines Amazon Foundation Models (Nova and Titan) as AI Services and explicitly names Nova Premier in section 50.10. The Premier service card points to these terms; the model is offered under proprietary service terms rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: Nova Premier — Amazon Bedrock (indexed page; live URL redirects)
sources.evidence: Search-indexed first-party page says launch October 31, 2025, Reasoning Supported, 1M context, 25K output, and conflicting lifecycle dates. Opening the URL redirected to the Bedrock guide root, so its current content was not accessible. Indexed launch/reasoning claims conflict with the dated GA announcement and parameter-specific Nova v1 schema; no endpoint/lifecycle conclusion is drawn.

name.note: Amazon Nova Premier is the official model name; the existing short name is accurate.

developer.note: Released by Amazon; technical report authored by Amazon Artificial General Intelligence.

family.note: The launch explicitly adds Premier to the Amazon Nova family.

release_date.note: Explicit dated GA announcement is primary evidence for earliest public release. Indexed October 31, 2025 claim is not the initial release and its page no longer opens; do not replace April 30.

open_weights.note: Proprietary Nova weights and managed API distribution. AWS escrow/customization access does not establish public weights; no Premier checkpoint release is documented in the reviewed primary sources.

license.note: Proprietary service terms govern the model. This is an access/license classification, not an SPDX open-weight license identifier.

parameters_b.note: No total parameter count is reported for Premier in its exact report, original family report or later Nova 2 comparison tables. Do not infer a count from relative tier, price or benchmark performance.

active_parameters_b.note: No per-token active parameter count is reported for Premier. Dense/MoE topology is also undisclosed, so no total-to-active equality is inferred.

architecture.note: The service card explicitly including Premier establishes Transformer-based token inference. Dense versus mixture-of-experts topology, expert counts and layer dimensions are not disclosed in the reviewed reports.

context_window.note: One million tokens, explicitly stated for the exact Premier model. Generic document-page context language does not supersede its model-specific table.

modalities.note: Exact model supports text/image/video input and text output; the v1 document guide explicitly includes Premier and PDFs. Audio is explicitly excluded by the launch and later comparison table despite its appearance in the shared schema.

reasoning.note: Dedicated extended-thinking support is unresolved. Current v1 parameter documentation restricts reasoningConfig to Pro and Lite, excluding Premier, while the exact-model Bedrock card preserved in the search index explicitly says Reasoning Supported. The latter now redirects, but that does not disprove its indexed specification. General reasoning capability and the launch comparison with non-reasoning models do not resolve this API-level conflict.

tool_call.note: The exact report evaluates function calling and the launch demonstrates agent/tool workflows; toolConfig is documented.

description.value: Multimodal model for complex analysis, long-context understanding, tool use, and model distillation
description.note: All listed capabilities are supported by the exact-model report and launch; the description makes no unsupported parameter, topology or dedicated thinking claim.

patch.notes: Transformer-based; total and active parameter counts and dense/MoE topology are undisclosed. Dedicated extended-thinking support is unresolved: the current Nova v1 reasoningConfig description excludes Premier, but an exact-model Bedrock card preserved in the search index says Reasoning Supported; its live URL now redirects. General reasoning ability does not resolve the conflict. The explicit April 30, 2025 GA announcement establishes initial release, despite the indexed card claiming a later launch date. This audit verifies documented specifications, not current endpoint availability.

summary: Added primary-source provenance, Transformer architecture and proprietary license classification. Confirmed Apr 30, 2025 GA, 1M context, text/image/video/PDF inputs, text output, tools and description. Total/active counts and dense/MoE topology remain undisclosed after original, Premier and later Nova 2 report checks. Cleared reasoning to null because the indexed exact-model card and current parameter-specific schema conflict on dedicated extended-thinking support.
